title: What are your thoughts on Mutiny On The Bounty (1962)?

commenti.body:
Did Brando ever say a bad thing about a woman? If so, we should cancel him and ban his movies.  

> I felt that Trevor Howard stole the show as William Bligh. I thought Brando was decent and didn't realized Richard Harris was in this.

However, I understand the issues, the film is long, longer than it should be. and Brando was just okay in this. I also feel that William Bligh gets the short end of the stick as, considering what I read on what happened, Bligh really wasn't a bad captain and was actually lenient, and I feel the downfall that cause the mutiny was the fact that they stay on Tahiti for too long, but hey Brando is the star and they needed the villain.

Though with this film, the film pretty much set back Brando's career because he was such a Prima donna behind the scenes and pretty much being impossible to work with pretty much everyone and charging the Studio with the most unnecessary requests. His career was pretty much almost dead until Coppola cast him for The Godfather.

All in All, What are your thoughts on the 1962 version of Mutiny On The Bounty?
don't say it don't say it don't say it

I was kind of meh on it, bordering on dislike. My husband and I are watching all of the top 100 greatest movies of all time and Mutiny on the Bounty was a few weeks ago for us. It was between The Great Dictator and Stagecoach which I think did it a favor rating wise for me, because if I watched it right after say Third Man or Good Will Hunting, it would have been such a different level of enjoyment for me I wouldn’t have ranked it on my top ten list at all. 

That being said, I think the way they filmed on location and the emotional development of some of the characters was enough to redeem this movie for me. Not a bucket list watch, but worth it if you have the time and want to see a visually groundbreaking movie then I’d watch. 

Ps- some of it is just brutal to sit through, though some would say that is part of what makes the movie what it is.

I like the Anthony Hopkins-Mel Gibson version bet. Thre vacillating men and their quickness to bitterness. Gibson and Hopkins both nail the internalize honor of the officer class and the duty to serve, though it goes sideways for each man at different turns. 

I usually dont go for naval stories but this one caught my attention and then I rewatched it 3 times while it cycled through a movie channel's schedule one week
